messages.content: Quick intro: I'm Max Turnquist, a robotics engineer.
I picked the violin back up this year and practice most evenings.
I adopted a cat named Biryani, a little tabby with opinions.
Palak paneer is my favorite food, total comfort dish.
I'm reading The Overstory by Richard Powers right now.
I ride a Cannondale Synapse road bike on weekends.
I'm learning Japanese before a trip to Kyoto in November.
Most weekends I go hiking in the foothills.
My coffee order is always a flat white.
My favorite movie is Arrival; I rewatch it constantly.
Radiohead is my favorite band by a mile.
I shoot photos with a Fujifilm X100V.
My go-to cocktail is a negroni.
I keep a fiddle-leaf fig in the living room.
I listen to the Lex Fridman podcast on commutes.
My sister Anita flew in to visit last week.
My parents, Deepak and Sunita, still live back in Portland.
My best friend Lena and I have known each other since school.
Anita and her husband Raj live in Chicago.
My manager at work, Priyanka, runs a tight ship.
My old college roommate Diego crashed on my couch last month.
My niece Mira just turned six.
My grad-school mentor was Professor Okafor.
Raj — my brother-in-law — is a cardiologist at a big hospital.
My best friend Lena works at Stripe and lives in San Francisco.
Anita is an architect and designed a library downtown.
Mira is Anita's daughter, so I spoil her rotten.
My manager Priyanka has been at Cobalt Robotics for a decade.
Professor Okafor taught robotics and still publishes constantly.
I'm finally settled in Denver after moving from Portland last spring.
I left Northwind Logistics in March and now work at Cobalt Robotics.
Cobalt has me leading the perception team now.
I switched from an iPhone to a Pixel a few months ago.
I used to play soccer but these days I train for marathons.
I got promoted to senior engineer at the last review.
I traded my old Civic for a Subaru Outback this year.
We moved out of our apartment into a small house in the spring.
I went vegetarian last year after decades of eating meat.
I recently got engaged to my partner Sam.
I climb at the Mesa Rim gym twice a week.
Autumn is hands down my favorite season.
I've been a Portland Trail Blazers fan my whole life.
Sam, my fiancé, is a veterinarian at a clinic called Brightpath Animal Hospital.
Sam and I first met at the Mesa Rim climbing gym, actually.
Sam plays the viola in a community orchestra.
My best friend Lena's partner is named Theo.
Theo is a pastry chef and runs a little bakery-cafe.
Lena grew up in Vancouver before she moved to the Bay Area.
At Stripe, Lena's actual role is product designer.
Anita's architecture firm is called Hargrove & Field.
Besides Mira, my sister Anita has a younger son — my nephew Felix.
Felix just turned three and is obsessed with dinosaurs.
My brother-in-law Raj works at Meridian General hospital.
Raj is a serious tennis player and competes most weekends.
Raj grew up in London and came here for his medical residency.
Before Cobalt, my manager Priyanka spent years at Lumen Labs.
Priyanka did her PhD at Caltech.
My old college roommate Diego is a lawyer now and lives in Montreal.
Diego and I both studied at Halford University.
Diego recently had a daughter named Ines.
Professor Okafor, my mentor, also teaches at Halford University.
Halford University is in Montreal.
Okafor just won an award called the Turing Robotics Prize.
My niece Mira is learning the harp.
Mira does gymnastics every Saturday.
My grandmother, Nana Rose, lives in a retirement community back in Portland.
Nana Rose was a concert pianist in her younger years.
My uncle on my mom's side, Bashir, runs a bakery in Portland.
Our perception team's flagship project is a warehouse robot codenamed Magpie.
On the team I work most closely with my teammate Imani.
Imani joined Cobalt from an aerospace company called Aerolith.
I wear a Garmin watch to track my marathon training.
My work laptop is a ThinkPad, but at home I use a Mac.
I started a running club with my friend Yusuf.
My dentist, Dr. Cardoza, has been seeing me for years.
My comfort TV show is The Bear; I've watched it three times.
The favorite city I've ever traveled to is Lisbon.
I'm allergic to penicillin — found out the hard way as a kid.
My favorite dessert is crème brûlée.
My favorite holiday is Diwali.
I recently started taking surfing lessons on weekends.
I collect vintage film cameras — got three on a shelf.
Funny enough, I'm afraid of heights, despite all the climbing.
I drink my tea with oat milk, never dairy.
I could play Catan every night; it's my favorite board game.
For years I coded mostly in C++, but at Cobalt I've switched to Rust.
I wore glasses for years but got LASIK last spring.
I used to live alone, but Sam moved in with me last year.
I quit smoking five years ago after a decade of it.
I deleted all my social media this year.
My friend Priya Sharma currently lives in Phoenix; she moved there from Eugene last spring.
Priya works at Verdant Automata now as a perception engineer; she left Borealis Freight back in March.
At Verdant Automata, Priya leads the perception team.
Priya's official job title at Verdant Automata is now Principal Perception Engineer — she got promoted from Senior Engineer in April.
Priya's husband is named Arjun Mehta.
Arjun is a structural engineer at a firm called Halcyon Bridgeworks in Phoenix.
Arjun plays the harmonium and sings at their temple on weekends.
Arjun grew up in Nairobi and moved to the US for grad school.
Priya and Arjun got married in Udaipur four years ago.
Priya's parents are Mohan and Lalita Sharma, and they still live in Eugene.
Priya's father Mohan is a retired botany professor.
Priya's mother Lalita runs a small textile shop called Marigold Looms.
Priya's grandmother, whom she calls Naani Asha, lives with her parents in Eugene.
Naani Asha was a radio playback singer in Lucknow when she was young.
Priya's older sister is Kavya, and she's an architect.
Kavya lives in Boston with her husband Vikram.
Last year Kavya designed a public library in Boston.
Kavya and Vikram have two kids: Priya's niece Tara and her nephew Kiran.
Priya's niece Tara is twelve and is a competitive figure skater.
Priya's nephew Kiran is eight and is obsessed with building marble runs.
Priya's brother-in-law Vikram — Kavya's husband — is a cardiologist.
Vikram works at a hospital called Lakeshore Cardiac Center in Boston.
Vikram is an avid open-water swimmer and does a relay across the lake every summer.
Priya also has a younger brother named Rohan.
Rohan is a marine biologist at the Coralline Institute.
Rohan lives in Kochi, in India.
Rohan is married to Priya's sister-in-law Fatima, who is a documentary filmmaker.
Rohan and Fatima have a baby daughter named Zoya.
Priya's best friend is Bianca, and she works at Plaid.
Bianca is a staff product manager at Plaid.
Bianca lives in Oakland and commutes across the bay.
Priya and Bianca met in college, where they were both on the rowing team.
Priya's close friend Meera Iyer is a pediatrician.
Meera works at Saint Brigid Hospital in Phoenix.
Meera owns a Bernese mountain dog named Laddoo.
Priya and Meera do a pottery class together on Thursday evenings.
Priya's friend Gabriel Okonkwo is a wine sommelier.
Gabriel runs the wine program at a restaurant in Reykjavik.
Gabriel was Priya's roommate during her exchange semester abroad.
Priya's manager at Verdant Automata is named Helena Vance.
Helena was an astronaut candidate before she went into the robotics field.
On the perception team, Priya works most closely with her teammate Oscar Mbeki.
Oscar joined Verdant Automata from a drone company called Skylark Dynamics.
Priya's mentor from grad school, Dr. Nadia Brandt, teaches at Rutgers.
Priya's cat is named Pumpkin, a little tabby with strong opinions.
Pumpkin is the only pet Priya has — just the one cat.
Priya adopted Pumpkin from a shelter called Mile-High Rescue.
Priya rides a Trek Domane road bike.
Priya drives a Rivian R1S — it's electric.
Priya plays the violin; she picked it back up after years.
Priya's everyday watch is a Withings ScanWatch.
Priya is reading Cloud Atlas by David Mitchell right now.
Priya's comfort show is Schitt's Creek — she's rewatched it four times.
Priya's favorite film of all time is Spirited Away.
Priya's go-to karaoke song is Mr. Brightside.
Priya is completely hooked on a podcast called Ologies.
Priya's favorite food is palak paneer — total childhood comfort food for her.
Priya's favorite dessert is gulab jamun.
Priya is allergic to shellfish; she found out the hard way at a wedding.
Priya takes her chai with cardamom and no sugar.
Priya is strictly vegetarian and has been her whole life.
Priya enjoys hiking — she did the Mount Falcon trail her first weekend in Phoenix.
Priya has recently taken up indoor rock climbing at a gym called Summit Stone.
Priya keeps a beehive on their rooftop and harvests honey in the fall.
Priya is terrified of deep open water, ironic given her brother's job.
Priya is learning Korean for a trip to Seoul in November.
Priya collects vintage fountain pens — she has about a dozen.
Priya used to commute on an old Vespa scooter, but now she drives her Rivian.
For years Priya's daily phone was a BlackBerry, but she switched to a OnePlus last year.
Priya used to code mostly in MATLAB, but at Verdant Automata she works almost entirely in Julia now.
Priya lived with three roommates in Eugene, but now she lives just with her husband Arjun in Phoenix.
Priya gave up coffee two years ago and switched entirely to chai.
Priya used to wear contact lenses, but she got PRK the year before last and ditched them.
Priya's old laptop was a clunky Dell, but her work machine now is a Framework laptop.
Priya was learning the sitar for a while, but she set it aside and went back to the violin.
Priya used to run marathons, but a knee injury pushed her toward cycling instead.
Priya quit biting her nails after twenty years — she finally kicked it last winter.
Priya's favorite season is autumn, hands down.
Priya is a green-tea-over-everything kind of person, but chai is her real love.
Priya's lucky number is seven.
Priya volunteers monthly at an engineering club for middle-schoolers called GearWorks.
Priya left Borealis Freight, where she had been a logistics systems engineer, back in March.
My friend Jordan Rivera is a senior software engineer, and he lives in Austin, Texas.
Jordan grew up in Miami but he's been in Austin for about three years now.
Jordan goes to the Austin Bouldering Project pretty regularly to climb.
Jordan rescued a greyhound named Mochi about a year ago.
Jordan works at Cumbre AI, where they're in the middle of a big Go migration.
Jordan's team was a Python shop but switched to Go for the backend about six months ago.
Jordan has been at Cumbre AI for two years, and he just got promoted to Senior Engineer a couple months ago.
Jordan's brother Rafael is a PM at Google and lives in Seattle.
Jordan's parents, Elena and Carlos, live in Miami and love visiting him in Austin.
Jordan's best friend is Valentina, who is in Phoenix working at Palantir; they met at PyCon 2021 in Salt Lake City.
Jordan has been re-reading Project Hail Mary and practices guitar in the evenings.
Jordan has played acoustic guitar for about ten years, and his favorite author is Ted Chiang — he loves Story of Your Life.
Jordan speaks intermediate Spanish and is saving up for a Japan trip he's planning for October.
Jordan's favorite food is tacos al pastor, and he raves about a spot near his office.
Jordan finally bought a Specialized Diverge for gravel riding around Austin.
Before Cumbre AI, Jordan spent four years at a fintech startup called Larkspur Pay.
At Larkspur Pay Jordan was a mid-level backend engineer, not yet senior.
Jordan's manager at Cumbre AI is named Adaeze Nwosu, and she's the VP of Engineering.
Adaeze Nwosu did her undergrad at Georgia Tech.
Cumbre AI's headquarters is in Austin, but it was originally founded in Toronto.
Jordan's team at Cumbre AI is the Recommendations team, and their main product is codenamed Driftwood.
Jordan writes Go on the backend and uses React on the frontend day to day.
In Houston, before he moved to Austin, Jordan lived in the Montrose district.
Back in Houston Jordan rented a tiny studio apartment, but in Austin he bought a small bungalow.
Jordan's neighborhood in Austin is called Travis Heights, just south of the river.
When Jordan lived in Houston he worked at Larkspur Pay, whose office was downtown.
Jordan's wife's name is Noor Haddad, and they got married four years ago.
Noor is an emergency room physician at Dell Seton Medical Center in Austin.
Noor grew up in Amman, Jordan, and moved to the US for medical school.
Jordan and Noor met at a tango class about seven years ago.
Noor is the only doctor in Jordan's family.
Besides his brother Rafael, Jordan has a younger sister named Lucia Rivera.
Lucia is a marine biologist and works at the Monterey Bay Aquarium.
Lucia lives in Monterey, California.
Lucia has a daughter — Jordan's niece — named Camila, who is six.
Camila is completely obsessed with sea turtles, thanks to her mom.
Rafael, Jordan's brother, has a son named Mateo — Jordan's nephew — who is nine.
Mateo plays in a youth soccer league and is the goalkeeper.
Jordan's grandmother on his dad's side, whom the family calls Abuela Marta, lives in Tampa, Florida.
Abuela Marta was a seamstress who ran her own tailoring shop for decades.
Rafael's wife — Jordan's sister-in-law — is named Yuki Tanaka, and she's a UX researcher at Microsoft.
Yuki Tanaka grew up in Calgary, Canada.
Jordan's closest friend at work is a colleague named Devon Ellison.
Devon Ellison is a machine learning engineer, also at Cumbre AI.
Devon moved to Austin from New Orleans, where he grew up.
Jordan's oldest friend from childhood is Hector Morales — they've known each other since middle school.
Hector Morales is a high school chemistry teacher in Orlando, Florida.
Jordan has a cycling buddy named Greta Lindqvist who races competitively.
Greta Lindqvist is a veterinarian and runs her own small-animal clinic.
Mochi the greyhound is Jordan's only dog, but he also has a tabby cat named Pelusa.
Pelusa the cat is fourteen years old — Jordan has had her since college.
Those two, Mochi and Pelusa, are Jordan's only pets.
Jordan drives a 2019 Toyota 4Runner that he takes camping.
Jordan's everyday phone is a Samsung Galaxy S24.
For photography Jordan shoots with an Olympus OM-1 mirrorless camera.
Jordan wears a Coros Apex watch when he's cycling and hiking.
Outside of guitar, Jordan's hobbies are gravel cycling, bouldering, sea kayaking, and birdwatching.
Jordan's favorite band is Khruangbin, and he's seen them live three times.
Jordan's comfort movie is Coherence — fitting, since he loves Ted Chiang.
Jordan's favorite video game is Hollow Knight.
Jordan is a huge fan of the TV show Severance.
Jordan's go-to board game is Wingspan, which pairs well with his birdwatching.
Jordan is allergic to shellfish, which makes coastal trips a little nerve-wracking for him.
Jordan is also lactose intolerant, so he drinks his coffee with almond milk.
Jordan is mildly colorblind — red-green — which his designer friends never let him forget.
Jordan's favorite dessert is tres leches cake, an old family recipe from Abuela Marta.
Jordan's favorite holiday is Nochebuena, Christmas Eve, when his whole family cooks together.
Jordan is terrified of deep open water, which is ironic given the kayaking.
Jordan used to drive a Honda Element for years, but he replaced it with his Toyota 4Runner last year.
Jordan's old phone was an iPhone 11, but he switched to a Samsung Galaxy S24 this spring.
Jordan used to live with three roommates in Houston, but now he lives with just his wife Noor.
For backend Jordan used to write Python, but he switched to Go about six months ago.
Jordan used to study Portuguese in college, but these days he's focused on learning Spanish instead.
Jordan quit drinking coffee for years and was a strict tea person, but he went back to coffee when he started at Cumbre AI.
Jordan used to use a Windows desktop for everything, but he switched to a MacBook Pro two years ago.
Jordan gave up running after a knee injury and took up cycling as his main cardio instead.
Jordan used to be a vegetarian, but now he just eats pescatarian — minus the shellfish he's allergic to.
Jordan's main editor used to be Vim, but he moved to VS Code when he joined Cumbre AI.
Jordan was the best man at his brother Rafael's wedding.
Jordan's blood type is O negative, so the blood bank loves him.
Jordan is an early riser — he's usually up by 5:30 for a ride before work.
Jordan's coffee order is a flat white with almond milk.
Jordan named his dog Mochi after his favorite childhood dessert, before tres leches took over.
Jordan just turned 34 this year.
Jordan's best friend Valentina Cruz works as a data scientist over at Palantir in Phoenix.
